title: Star Clusters Born in the Wreckage of Cosmic Collisions
caption: The center of Stephan's Quintet, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Stephan's Quintet · constellation Pegasus · about 300 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA/ESA, Jayanne English (University of Manitoba), Sally Hunsberger (Pennsylvania State University), Zolt Levay ( Space Telescope Science Institute), Sarah Gallagher (Pennsylvania State University), and Jane Charlton (Pennsylvania State University)

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: Twisted shapes, dust lanes stretching between galaxies and long strands of stars and gas reaching far beyond the central regions all point to violent encounters. This Hubble close-up shows the central part of Stephan's Quintet, a group of galaxies molded by tidal interactions, and, according to the source, one of the most exciting star-forming regions in the local Universe.

The quintet is the prototype of the class called compact groups of galaxies, and astronomers have studied it intensively for decades. It is a favorite of amateur astronomers and a challenging target for good hobby telescopes. It even appears, as angelic figures, at the start of the 1946 film It's a Wonderful Life.

At least two of the galaxies have been through high-speed, hit-and-run collisions that ripped stars and gas from their neighbors and flung them into space. New life has come from the wreckage. Over 100 star clusters have emerged from it, along with several dwarf galaxies.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.28 x 3.57 arcminutes) and distance (300 million light years), the frame spans roughly 199,000 × 312,000 light-years. Its light set out about 300 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 observed the group in visible and near-infrared light, through filters at 450, 569 and 814 nm. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Through a good hobby telescope the quintet is a challenging, faint target, and Hubble reveals star clusters and filaments no eye could see.

explore: The young clusters each hold up to millions of stars. Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 showed them clearly for the first time.
alt: Several distorted galaxies close together, linked by dust lanes and long streams of stars and gas.
